rules.title: A thesis for the doctoral degree must constitute original scholarship and must be a distinct contribution to knowledge

6 credits, at the 500, 600, or 700 level, selected from courses within and/or outside the department relevant to the student's research area and in consultation with the student's supervisor and advisory committee
At least 3 of the 6 credits must also be pre-approved by the Neotropical Environment Director
A maximum of 24 credits at the 500 level or higher can be taken inside or outside the Department (e.g., language training, methodological training, history or regional studies courses)
The purpose of the language requirement is to ensure that the student has access to anthropological literature in at least two languages

In addition to the above requirements, 15 credits from courses at the 500 level or higher within and/or outside of the Department relevant to the student’s research area in consultation with the student’s supervisor and/or PhD committee
